analysis:
This PR changes documentation only. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md, the head adds one row at line 1732 to the daemon environment passthrough table: DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS, read in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillChunkKey, stepTokenBudgetKey). In docs/reference/configuration.md (line 379 hunk), the head replaces the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE row with a PREFILL_CHUNK row. I could not see the rest of that patch or any head text for that file.

Security assessment: these are scheduler and performance tunables for token chunk and step sizes. They are not secrets, keys, attestation inputs, authorization inputs, cache scope inputs, or crypto parameters. The documented passthrough only copies shell values into the LaunchAgent plist at `darkbloom start`. The operator is already the owner of that plist (TB-003). A local operator could already change these values. I found no evidence that the passthrough crosses a trust boundary the coordinator relies on, or that it touches A-001, A-003, A-016, T-041 or the prefix cache/KEK/TTL/HMAC posture.

Remaining uncertainty: the actual Swift source for passthroughEnvKeys and the Configuration.swift bounds checks is not supplied. I cannot confirm that the code matches the doc (that is, that these keys are really forwarded, and that values are range-validated so extreme chunk sizes cannot cause memory exhaustion or DoS). The impact would be limited to operator self-harm on the operator's own provider. The configuration.md patch is truncated, and no head text is supplied for that file. Integration should check that the code change adding the passthrough clamps values, and that no cache-affecting or attestation-affecting variable was added to the passthrough list.

No findings.
